chapter: Western University and Kansas City nightlife
title: Switching from tuba to bass in the Western storeroom
summary: He took a string bass and a saxophone from a storeroom of old band instruments, with Guy Taylor in charge.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: Yeah. Well, so in a sense, you sort of--you picked up your knowledge as you went along?
Yeah. In fact, when I got to Kansas City, I was still a tuba player, sousaphone player.
Well, when did you make the switch?
Well, actually, I made the switch in '33. But I didn't have nerve enough to go out into the opening and do it. I did it with my band there, you know, until late '34.
Well, how did you find that transition? I mean, did you--
Well, it was enjoyable. I tell

what I did. you They had a storeroom that was about a hundred by a hundred in diameter. And the ceiling and all the walls were just lined with musical instruments, where Western had had great bands in the past. And all these instruments were here, and the guy said, 'Well, if you want an instrument, get it.' So I took a bass. I came back, and asked him could I have a saxophone. So I was learning saxophone and studying that bass at the same time, myself.
They'd had a real big band there?
They had had, at one time.

And, see, that's Guieu (phon Guieu) Taylor, you may have heard of Guieu Taylor. He was a good violin player who worked with Basie at the Avalon Theatre. And he was in charge of the music department. So, he was the director of the band. Naturally, we had a pretty good size-- we had about a 18-piece marching band, you know. And we played for the assembly every morning, in fact, about eight of us-- The Lord's Prayer and a couple of tunes, 'Indian Dawn,' and we played 'Hungarian Rhapsody,' things like that.
Yeah. Well, I mean this was all very good for you.
Yeah, it was a good foundation for me, the experience and the learning at the same time.
